title: India Reopens Tourist Visas for Bangladesh After a Two-Year Freeze — and the Kolkata–Dhaka Corridor Exhales
excerpt: Starting June 28, India will issue tourist visas to Bangladeshi nationals again, ending a suspension rooted in the fall of Sheikh Hasina. For the Bengali diaspora in the US, the thaw reopens a cross-border family lifeline just ahead of pujo season.
body:
India will resume tourist visa services for Bangladeshi nationals on June 28, ending a nearly two-year period of restricted travel. The announcement, made by India's High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Pranay Verma, at a media briefing in Dhaka on Thursday, signals a significant step in the ongoing normalization of India-Bangladesh relations.

For the Bengali diaspora scattered across the United States — concentrated in the New York-New Jersey metro, Houston, the Dallas-Fort Worth corridor, and the Bay Area — the thaw quietly reopens something more personal than a diplomatic channel: the family corridor between Kolkata and Dhaka. This resumption of travel facilitates easier visits for NRIs with family ties in both nations, impacting everything from holiday plans to medical support for relatives.

## What Was Restricted, and Why


![Pranay Verma — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/24/Pranay_Verma_in_2024_%28PID-0008527%29_%28cropped%5E2%29.jpg)


While a complete freeze on tourist visas was not officially declared, the processing of such visas became significantly more stringent and slow following the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent geopolitical shifts. India had prioritized medical visas and certain categories of business travel, processing them on a case-by-case basis. However, the mass tourist channel — used by hundreds of thousands of Bangladeshis visiting India annually for everything from Durga Puja pilgrimages to medical treatment in Kolkata hospitals — saw a substantial reduction in approvals.



> **"The Petrapole-Benapole land border — roughly 80 kilometers from Kolkata — handles millions of crossings annually in normal times."**


The political landscape has seen ongoing developments. Bangladesh, under Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's government, has been navigating its relationships with both India and China. High Commissioner Verma's visa announcement comes amidst continued diplomatic engagements between Bangladesh and its key regional partners, reflecting a broader effort to strengthen bilateral ties.

## The Kolkata-Dhaka Corridor


![Bay Area — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/OAKLAND%2C_CA%2C_USA_-_Skyline_and_Bridge.JPG/3840px-OAKLAND%2C_CA%2C_USA_-_Skyline_and_Bridge.JPG)


The India-Bangladesh border is one of South Asia's busiest people-to-people crossings. The Petrapole-Benapole land border — roughly 80 kilometers from Kolkata — handles millions of crossings annually in normal times. Kolkata's Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport serves as the primary air gateway, with multiple daily flights to Dhaka, Chittagong, and Sylhet.

The restrictions on tourist visas significantly disrupted this flow. Medical tourism, which drives a significant portion of Bangladeshi travel to India — particularly to hospitals in Kolkata, Chennai, and Vellore — slowed considerably. Religious pilgrimages to Kolkata's Kalighat and Dakshineswar temples, a fixture of the Bengali Hindu calendar on both sides of the border, were curtailed. Cultural exchange — literary festivals, theatrical collaborations, academic conferences — also faced hurdles.

The resumption of tourist visas does not instantly restore pre-pandemic volumes. Visa processing infrastructure needs to ramp back up, and applicants will face the usual queue at Indian missions in Dhaka and Chittagong. But the signal is considerable: India is reopening, and the corridor is coming back to life.


![Durga Puja — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0_%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%80%E0%A6%A8_%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%97%E0%A7%8B%E0%A7%8E%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%AC_%E0%A7%A8%E0%A7%A6%E0%A7%A7%E0%A7%AE.jpg/3840px-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0_%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%80%E0%A6%A8_%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%97%E0%A7%8B%E0%A7%8E%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%AC_%E0%A7%A8%E0%A7%A6%E0%A7%A7%E0%A7%AE.jpg)


## The NRI Dimension

This matters to the Indian American community in ways the headline does not capture. Bengali Americans — among the larger South Asian sub-communities in the US — often maintain extended family networks that span both Kolkata and Dhaka. Partition-era migrations, intermarriage, and shared cultural traditions mean that a single family's Durga Puja gathering might draw relatives from Jackson Heights, Salt Lake (Kolkata), and Dhanmondi (Dhaka).

During the period of restricted visas, NRIs planning India visits could not easily coordinate family reunions that included Bangladeshi relatives. A Kolkata wedding that would normally draw guests from Dhaka had to proceed without them. A medical consultation at a Kolkata hospital that a Bangladeshi relative needed became a bureaucratic ordeal rather than a routine border crossing. The inability for family members to travel freely also impacted remittances and financial support, as direct visits often facilitate these exchanges.

With tourist visas resuming June 28, these barriers drop. NRIs flying to Kolkata this autumn — and the festive season from Durga Puja through Diwali is peak travel time — can once again plan gatherings that include family from across the border. This also eases the logistical burden for dual citizens or those with family in both countries who previously faced challenges in coordinating international travel.

The diplomatic context remains dynamic, with India and Bangladesh continuously engaging on various fronts. But for the Bengali diaspora, the geopolitics is secondary. What matters is that the corridor between Kolkata and Dhaka is open again — just in time for pujo season.
